﻿ INTRUSION The act of gaining unauthorized access to a system so as to cause loss or harm.
The most common threat to security is an attack by an Intruder.
Intruders may be from outside the network or legitimate users of the network.

﻿ INTRUDERS Intruders are often referred to as hackers
Exploits the vulnerability; most harmful factor contributing to the breach of security.
They have immense knowledge and an in-depth understanding of technology and security. 
Intruders breach the privacy of users and aim to steal the confidential information of the users. 
The stolen information is then sold to third parties, which aim at misusing the information for their own personal or professional gains. 
Intruders can broadly be divided into 3 different types: Masquerader, Misfeasor, Clandestine Users

﻿ INTRUDER TYPES Masquerader
The category of individuals that are not authorized to use the system but still exploit user’s privacy and confidential information by possessing techniques that give them control over the system. 
Masqueraders are outsiders and hence they don’t have direct access to the system, their aim is to attack unethically to steal data/ information.
Misfeasor
The category of individuals that are authorized to use the system, but misuse the granted access and privilege. 
These are individuals that take undue advantage of the permissions and access given to them.
Misfeasors are insiders and they have direct access to the system, which they aim to attack unethically for stealing data/ information.

﻿ INTRUDER TYPES Clandestine Users
The category of individuals who have supervision/administrative control over the system and misuse the authoritative power given to them. 
The misconduct of power is often done by superlative authorities for financial gains
A Clandestine User can be any of the two, insiders or outsiders, and accordingly, they can have direct/ indirect access to the system, which they aim to attack unethically for stealing data/ information.

﻿ INTRUSION PREVENTION SYSTEM (IPS) Intrusion prevention is the process of detecting the signs of intrusion and attempting to stop the intrusive efforts.
It is more advanced than an intrusion detection system (IDS).

﻿ INTRUSION DETECTION SYSTEM (IDS) Inevitably, the best intrusion prevention system tends to fail. 
A system's second line of defence is intrusion detection, and this has been the focus of much research in recent years.  This interest is motivated by a number of considerations:
If an intrusion is detected quickly enough, the intruder can be identified and ejected from the system before any damage is done or any data is compromised. 
An effective intrusion detection system can serve as a deterrent (barrier), acting to prevent intrusions.
Intrusion detection enables the collection of information about intrusion techniques that can be used to strengthen the intrusion prevention facility.

﻿ INTRUSION DETECTION SYSTEM (IDS) Intrusion Detection System (IDS) monitors network traffic for unusual or suspicious activity and sends an alert to the administrator. 
Detection of anomalous activity and reporting it to the network administrator is the primary function 
Some IDS software can take action based on rules when malicious activity is detected, for example blocking certain incoming traffic.
Intrusion detection systems are of two types:
Network based 
Host-based
﻿ NETWORK BASED IDS (NIDS)

﻿ NETWORK BASED IDS (NIDS) NIDS usually has two logical components: the sensor and the management station. 
The sensors are usually dedicated systems that exist only to monitor the network.
Sensors  have an network interface in promiscuous mode. 
If they detect something that looks unusual, they pass it to the management station.
The management station can display the alarms or do additional analysis.
﻿ NETWORK BASED IDS (NIDS)

﻿ NETWORK BASED IDS (NIDS) Strengths
NIDS can detect some of the attacks that use the network. 
A network-based IDS does not require modification of servers or hosts. 
The IDS is not placed on a critical path for any production services or processes because a network-based IDS does not act as a router or other critical device. 
Network-based IDS systems tend to be more self-contained than host-based systems.

﻿ NETWORK BASED IDS (NIDS) Weaknesses
NIDS only examines network traffic on the segment to which it is directly connected, but it cannot detect an attack that travels through a different network segment. 
NIDS tend to use signature analysis in order to meet performance requirements. 
A NIDS may need to communicate large volumes of data back to the central analysis system. The disadvantage of this is that it provides very little coordination amongst sensors.
A network-based IDS may have a difficult time handling attacks within encrypted sessions.

﻿ HOST BASED IDS (HIDS) HIDS looks for signs of intrusion on the local host system. 
These frequently use the host system’s audit and logging mechanism as a source of information for analysis.
They look for unusual activity that is confined to the local host such as logins, improper file access, unapproved privilege escalation, or alterations on system privileges. 
This IDS architecture generally uses rule-based engines for analysing activity.

﻿ HOST BASED IDS (HIDS) Strengths
HIDS can be an extremely powerful tool for analysing a possible attack. 
Host-based systems tend to have lower false positive rates than network-based systems. 
Host based systems can be used in environments where broad intrusion detection is not needed.
A host-based system is less risky to configure with an active response, such as terminating a service or logging off an offending user.

﻿ HOST BASED IDS (HIDS) Weaknesses
HIDS require installation on the particular device that you wish to protect. 
HIDS tend to rely on the innate logging and monitoring capabilities of the server. 
HIDS are relatively expensive. 
HIDS suffer to an even greater degree, from local-vision restrictions. The analysis time required to evaluate damage from a potential intrusion increases linearly with the number of protected hosts.

﻿ INTRUSION DETECTION TECHNIQUES All IDSs use two modes of operation 
Signature-based IDS
Anomaly-based IDS
Some may only use one or the other, but most use both.

﻿ SIGNATURE BASED IDS In this technique, the sensors which are placed in different LAN segments filter and analyse network packets in real time and compares them against a database of known attack signatures. 
Attack signatures are known methods that intruders have employed in the past to penetrate a network. 
The signature-based method looks at checksums and message authentication. 
A HIDS will look at log and config files for any unexpected rewrites
A NIDS will look at the checksums in captured packets and message authentication integrity of systems such as SHA1.
The NIDS may include a database of signatures that packets known to be sources of malicious activities carry.

﻿ ANOMALY BASED IDS Anomaly-based detection looks for unexpected or unusual patterns of activities. 
This category can be implemented by both host and network-based intrusion detection systems. 
In case of HIDS, an anomaly might be repeated failed login attempts or unusual activity on the ports of a device that signify port scanning.
In the case of NIDS, the anomaly approach requires establishing a baseline of behaviour to create a standard situation against which ongoing traffic patterns can be compared. 
A range of traffic patterns are considered acceptable, and when current real-time traffic moves out of that range, an anomaly alert is provoked.
﻿ FIREWALL A firewall is a device that filters all traffic between a protected or “inside” network and less trustworthy or “outside” network.

﻿ Characteristics of Firewall All traffic from inside to outside and vice versa, must pass through the firewall. 
To achieve this, all the access to the local network must first be physically blocked and access only via the firewall should be permitted.
Only the traffic authorized as per the local security policy should be allowed to pass through.
The firewall itself must be strong enough , so as to render attacks on itself.

﻿ TYPES OF FIREWALL Packet filters
Stateful  packet filters
Application proxies
Personal firewalls

﻿ PACKET FILTER FIREWALL A packet filter applies a set of rules to each packet and based on the outcome, decides to either forward or discard the packet.
It is also called as a screening router or screening filter.
The filtering rules are based on a number of fields in the IP and TCP/UDP headers.
A packet filter performs the following functions:
Receive each packet as it arrives.
Pass the packet through a set of rules, based on the contents of the IP and transport header fields of the packet.
If there is no match with any rule, take the default action.

﻿ PACKET FILTER FIREWALL Advantages:
Application independent - only examines packet at the network layer
High performance - simple rules that require little processing and decision making beyond what is normally done for routing decisions
Scalable - low overhead of filtering means large amount of traffic can be handled
Transparent - user’s don’t need to provide additional passwords or use special commands to initiate connections

﻿ PACKET FILTER FIREWALL Disadvantages:
Examines and filters only at the network layer - no application level awareness or state context is maintained
Security is weak -  the state of a given connection is not maintained making it easier to exploit networking protocols and applications.

﻿ ATTACKS ON PACKET FILTER FIREWALL IP address spoofing
fake source address to be trusted
add filters on router to block

Source routing attacks
attacker sets a route other than default
block source routed packets

Tiny fragment attacks
split header information over several tiny packets
either discard or reassemble before check

﻿ STATEFUL PACKET FILTER FIREWALL A stateful packet filter adds state to a packet filter firewall. This means that the firewall keeps tracks of TCP connections, and it can remember UDP connections as well.
A stateful packet filter operates at the transport layer. 
The primary advantage of a stateful packet filter is that in addition to all the features of a  packet filter, it also keeps track of ongoing connection.
The disadvantage of  a stateful packet filter are that it cannot examine application data.
 It’s slower than a packet filtering firewall since more processing is required.

﻿ STATEFUL PACKET FILTER FIREWALL Advantages: 
Maintain a state table to track active connections.
Inspect packets in the context of their associated connection.
Make decisions based on both the packet header information and the state of the connection.
Can implement more sophisticated security policies, such as blocking unauthorized connections or detecting anomalies in traffic patterns.

﻿ STATEFUL PACKET FILTER FIREWALL Advantages: 
Improved security: Stateful packet filters can detect and block various attacks that packet filters might miss, such as SYN flood attacks and spoofing.
Enhanced performance: By maintaining state information, stateful packet filters can optimize their decision-making process and reduce the computational overhead.
Flexibility: Stateful packet filters can implement more complex security policies, such as allowing only established connections or blocking certain types of traffic based on the source or destination IP address.

﻿ APPLICATION PROXY A proxy is something that acts on your behalf.
An application proxy firewall processes incoming packets all the way up to the application layer.
The primary advantage of  the application proxy is that it has complete view of the connections and the application data.
The disadvantage of an application proxy is speed.
One interesting feature of an application proxy is that the incoming packet is destroyed and a new packet is created when the data passes through the firewall.

﻿ PERSONAL FIREWALL A personal firewall is used to protect a single host or  a small network, such as  a home network.
software applications that act as a security barrier between your computer and the internet.
Any of the three methods discussed earlier can be used. 
Generally such firewalls are relatively simple for the sake of efficiency.

﻿ Features of Personal Firewalls Inbound and Outbound Traffic Control: They can block or allow specific types of traffic, such as incoming connections from unknown sources or outgoing connections to potentially malicious websites.
Port Blocking: They can prevent unauthorized access to specific ports on your computer, which are used by various applications and services.
Intrusion Detection: Some firewalls can detect and alert you to potential hacking attempts or other malicious activities.
Application Control: They can restrict or block certain applications from accessing the internet, helping to prevent unauthorized downloads or data leaks.
Network Address Translation (NAT): This feature hides your computer's IP address from the internet, making it more difficult for hackers to target your system.

﻿ NETWORK ADDRESS TRANSLATION One of the interesting jobs done by a firewall is to perform Network Address Translation (NAT).

NAT attempts to solve the problem of the shortage of IP addresses.
NAT allows user to have a  large number of IP addresses internally , but only a single IP address externally.
It also hides your computer's IP address from the internet, making it more difficult for hackers to target your system.

﻿ FIREWALL CONFIGURATIONS & BASTION HOST A bastion host is a system, identified as a critical point in the network’s security. 
Typically, the bastion host serves as a platform for an application-level gateway.

﻿ BASTION HOST Characteristics Often a bastion host runs a single application or process.
Only the services that the network administrator considers essential are installed on the bastion host. 
Examples of Bastion host are proxy server, load balancer, mail, web, DNS servers etc.
Bastion host is exposed to the public network, hence must withstand cyber attacks. Its often equipped with special network interfaces.
The bastion host hardware platform executes a secure version of its operating system, making it a hardened system.
The bastion host may require additional authentication before a user is allowed access to the proxy services. In addition, each proxy service may require its own authentication before granting user access.
﻿ Firewall Configuration with Bastion The best method to secure bastion host, is to use two level firewall.

﻿ FIREWALL CONFIGURATIONS with Bastion Bastion host placement in the network is often associated with the firewall.
Following configurations are commonly used.
Screened Host Firewall, Single Homed Bastion
Screened Host Firewall, Dual Homed Bastion
Screened Subnet Firewall

﻿ SCREENED HOST FIREWALL, SINGLE HOMED BASTION In the Screened Host Firewall, Single Homed Bastion configuration,  a firewall set up consists of two parts,
A packet filtering router 
The packet filter ensures that the incoming traffic is allowed only if it is destined for the application gateway, by examining the destination address field of every incoming packet. 
Similarly, it also ensures that the outgoing traffic is allowed only if it is originating from the application gateway, by examining the source address field of every outgoing IP packet.
An application gateway
The application gateway performs authentication and proxy functions.
﻿ SCREENED HOST FIREWALL, SINGLE HOMED BASTION

﻿ SCREENED HOST FIREWALL, SINGLE HOMED BASTION Advantages:
This configuration increases the security of the network by performing checks at both packet and application levels.
This also gives more flexibility to the network administrators to define more granular security policies.
Disadvantage:
The internal users are connected to the bastion, as well as to the packet filter. 
If the packet filter is somehow successfully attacked and its security is compromised , then the whole internal network is exposed to the attacker.

﻿ SCREENED HOST FIREWALL, DUAL HOMED BASTION In this configurations, direct connections between the internal hosts and the packet filter are avoided. 
The packet filter now connects only to the bastion, which in turn has  a separate connection with the internal hosts.
Therefore, even if the packet filter is successfully attacked, only the bastion is visible to the attacker. 
The internal hosts are protected.
﻿ SCREENED HOST FIREWALL, DUAL HOMED BASTION

﻿ SCREENED SUBNET FIREWALL This is one of the most secured firewall configurations. 
In this configuration, two packet filtering routers are used, and the bastion host is positioned in between the two routers.
This creates a screened subnet between the two firewalls
﻿ SCREENED SUBNET (DMZ) FIREWALL

﻿ DEMILITARIZED ZONE (DMZ) NETWORKS A DMZ, or demilitarized zone, is a physical or logical subnet that separates a local area network (LAN) from other untrusted networks -- usually, the public internet. 
DMZs are also known as perimeter networks or screened subnetworks.
Servers and resources in the DMZ are accessible from the internet, but the rest of the internal LAN remains unreachable.
This approach provides an additional layer of security to the LAN as it restricts a hacker's ability to directly access internal servers and data from the internet.

﻿ Let’s Revise A packet filter firewall filters at __________.
Physical layer
Data link layer
Network layer or Transport layer
Application layer

What is the primary advantage of using a packet filter firewall?
High performance
Easy to configure
Low cost
All of the above

﻿ Let’s Revise What is the primary function of a packet filter firewall?
To inspect and filter network packets based on their headers.
To monitor network traffic for unauthorized access attempts.
To prevent unauthorized access to network resources.
To encrypt and decrypt data transmitted over the network.

Which of the following is NOT a common filtering criterion used by packet filter firewalls?
Source IP address
Destination IP address
Protocol
Application data

﻿ Let’s Revise What is the main limitation of packet filter firewalls?
They cannot inspect the contents of packets.
They are not effective against stateful attacks.
They cannot be used to protect against malware.
 They are difficult to configure.

Which type of firewall is considered more secure than a packet filter firewall?
Stateful inspection firewall
Application firewall
Proxy firewall
All of the above
